rationale: A .carbonwebgpu is a derived artifact, fully determined by (source bytes at a pinned build id + compiler version). Storing the package duplicates a guarantee the compiler already gives and rots silently when the compiler moves. This manifest pins the identity instead: rebuild, compare packageSha256, and a compiler change announces itself as a reviewable manifest diff. The rendered target bytes are pinned because they are the only part that needs a GPU to reproduce.
sourcePolicy: Source .sm_lo/.sm_hi/.sm_depth bytes are CCP game files. Never commit, fixture, or publish them. Fetch through tools-core at the pinned build id.

resourceTransformGates.detail: Merges Detail1Map and Detail2Map into one 2d-array binding in Detail1Map's slot. 22 logical bindings over 22 physical, 4096 pixels exact across 3 cases, both MRTs, both backends, 0 WGSL warnings; the detail control changed 570/635 covered pixels, so the assembled array is genuinely sampled.

The Avatar's family: merges Detail1/2/3Map into one three-layer 2d-array binding, so the layout is two bindings shorter than the reflection. Static changed 1116/1116 covered pixels for both detail controls; skinned changed 634/635 and 635/635 with indexed non-identity BoneTransforms observed. The Detail1 and Detail2 delta maps were distinct in both, which is what shows the layers are assembled in declared order and sampled independently rather than collapsed.
resourceTransformGates.note: The static body keeps SPACE_OBJECT_INSTANCED_ATTACHMENT in its permutation; the skinned body drops it. Building either with the wrong axis set fails the fixture's provenance check rather than producing a wrong package.

gatingAxes.summary: Two independent gates decide the Quad V5 Main binding inventory, and conflating them misattributes a body difference to the tier. Measured on dx11 at build 3444265, PPT-on, Main.pass0.

bodyGated.detail: Reached by V5_DEBUG=ON at Medium, which resolves body 28 rather than body 4. So these are NOT tier-exclusive.

tierGated.detail: Only .sm_depth binds the forward-light set. Medium never does, at any V5_DEBUG value.

gatingAxes.fixtureScope: Every fixture here pins body 4 at V5_DEBUG=OFF, so within that pin the tier alone determines the inventory and deriving expectations from the source-path suffix is sound. It would not be sound across V5_DEBUG values. Note the debug body is not merely 'body 4 plus dust': it carries 29 constants in 452 bytes against body 4 High's 24 in 384.

resourceTransformContract: Only kind texture-2d-array, version 1, representation native-or-rgba8, and missingLayer reject are realized. The transform record and the layout it claims to have rewritten are both validated, so a package cannot describe a merge the layout did not perform. The analysis is pre-transform and the layout is post-transform: a consumer that conflates them either over-binds or fails to fill the array.

staleness.reMeasured: 2026-08-13, runtime-resource 0.17.0, by test/wgsb-equivalence.test.js building in process from the pinned source bytes.
staleness.current: Every count under fixtures[quadv5-ppt-main].allBody. permutations and translationUnits are unchanged on both backends; dx12 uniqueBodies/unsupportedBodies moved and are re-pinned with their reason.
staleness.stale: Every packageSha256 and packageByteLength in this file, and every count under fixtures[quadv5-high-ppt-main]. They were measured before the Carbon v15 container replaced the chunk package, so the wire format itself changed: the medium dx11 every-body package is 3154661 bytes now against the 15054155 pinned here. They are retained as the historical record of what the previous compiler produced, and nothing asserts them.
staleness.policy: A number in this file is either asserted by a test or listed as stale. Do not add a third category: an unasserted, undated number reads as a pin and is how the engine came to be measured against a package nobody had rebuilt in weeks.

allBody.note: DX12 exposes bindless bodies that do not lower. They are retained as explicitly unsupported records with their reason; DX12 is comparison-only evidence.
allBody.uniqueBodiesNote: Was 288/144 before the container port. All 144 bodies that do not lower still exist as permutations, but an untranslated body emits no programs, so its record differs only by its Carbon description - and 144 such records share 49 distinct descriptions, which the container's alias rule collapses. No body is lost: translationUnits is still 144, which is why that is the count the test asserts and uniqueBodies is not.

gates.prepared: --prepare-carbonwebgpu and --prepare-bodyset are green at High: 25 canonical bindings per selected package, and all 168 all-body translation units, with 0 WGSL warnings
gates.drawn: npm run test:webgpu:required -- --draw-quadv5 <dx11.carbonwebgpu> <dx12.carbonwebgpu> with the .sm_depth pair: 25 logical bindings over 25 physical, 4096 pixels matched exactly across 1 case, both MRTs, and both backends with 0 WGSL warnings. The tier is derived from the package source-path suffix, so the same flag covers both tiers.

inventory.note: Uniform buffer sizes and the vertex layout are identical to Medium body 4. cb0 keeps the same 384-byte footprint and adds Mtl1..4DustDiffuseColor at offsets 224-287, which Medium body 4 leaves as a hole; packMaterial is reflection-driven and requires a value for every reflected constant, so a mismatch fails closed. The pixel interface adds TEXCOORD11 at register 10 (vec3) and the vertex output adds output10.

arrayTexture.name: LightProfileArray
arrayTexture.note: The WGSL type spells the dimension with an underscore where the WebGPU enum uses a hyphen. Realizing 2d-array textures is therefore a prerequisite for a High draw, not a follow-on to resource-transform support.

inventory.samplerNote: Carbon reflects s0 and s3 without a name, and DX12 lowers exactly those two unnamed samplers to immutable root-signature samplers. On the wire those carry a borderColor enum byte and no dynamic flag; the reader expands the enum to a float4 and restores isDynamic: false, so the reflected state is identical on both backends. s3 is not a copy of s0: minFilter 2, mipFilter 0, and clamped addressing on every axis.

textureRegisters.note: Contiguous on both backends for body 4. The holes at DX12 5 and 8 in the Medium record are a property of body 4, not of the Medium tier - see gatingAxes.

allBody.note: DX12 exposes bindless bodies that do not lower, matching the Medium pattern. They are retained as explicitly unsupported records with their reason; DX12 is comparison-only evidence.
